idiom_name: node:events EventEmitter (or DOM EventTarget) with frozen event objects
implementation_notes: Node's standard library supplies the dispatcher: an EventEmitter instance is the bus, emit(name, payload) publishes, on(name, handler) subscribes, and the event object is a frozen plain object (or a small class) named in the past tense. Nothing checks the names at compile time, so keep them in exported constants and build payloads in one factory per event. In browsers the same role is played by EventTarget.dispatchEvent with CustomEvent.detail, and frameworks ship their own emitters; the structure - event object, publisher, subscribers - is unchanged, and the classic hand-written registry is not needed.
pitfalls: Event names are runtime strings: a typo in on('order.placed') silently never fires - export constants and assert at startup that every declared event has at least one subscriber.
Emission is synchronous and re-entrant: a listener that emits again can recurse, and an exception in one listener prevents the later ones from running unless the error policy handles it.
